title: Health research funding — 9bn CZK with no impact evaluation and no institutional-support controls at all
money_note: 5.4bn CZK targeted plus 3.6bn CZK institutional health R&D support in 2020-2024 (the conclusion's own basic facts), 9.0bn CZK converted at 24.5 CZK/EUR
summary: NKU audit 25/13 found that for years the Health Ministry did not evaluate whether its 9bn CZK of health research programmes met their goals, only began collecting data on how results reach practice in 2025, paid project support late against statutory deadlines, and never controlled institutional support at all over its entire existence. It also failed to deliver the evaluation methodology the government ordered after the previous NKU audit 19/17 in 2019.
notes: Conclusion PDF parsed (SCANS.md demand-scan item 1). Responsible body: Ministerstvo zdravotnictvi, with Agentura pro zdravotnicky vyzkum (AZV) as the selecting agency; audited recipients VFN Praha, FN Brno, FN Olomouc. Approved by the NKU Kolegium at its VIII. session on 18 May 2026, resolution 5/VIII/2026; published with the NKU press release of 7 September 2026 (the record date). Basic facts: 521 targeted projects and 111 MZd controls of them; 19 institutional recipients and 0 MZd controls. The headline verdict is PARTLY POSITIVE and is stated so nobody reads this as a failed programme: AZV selected projects transparently and 37 of 41 checked projects had results used in practice. The record exists for the evaluation and control gap. The scripted nku feed staged the press-release headline as nku-15872 in data/raw/2026-09-08/staged.jsonl (pending, not in any ledger); this record is the conclusion-level reading of the same audit, and MATCH should treat the two as one audit.
quote: U institucionální podpory navíc MZd neprovádělo kontrolu vůbec – a to po celou dobu její existence.

title: IKEM procurement audit — law broken in half of 30 contracts, IT bought through 345 split orders
money_note: 380.1m CZK, the value of the 15 audited contracts in which IKEM broke the law (of 30 audited worth 578.7m CZK), converted at 24.5 CZK/EUR
summary: NKU audit 25/14 found that the Institute for Clinical and Experimental Medicine broke procurement law in 15 of 30 audited contracts, worth 380.1m CZK together, paid 59.5m CZK for IT services to three suppliers through at least 345 orders without any tender, and wrote off 77 percent of the audited scrapped assets without proper documents. NKU flagged 182.2m CZK in 17 cases as suspected breaches of budget discipline and found that IKEM's internal control system repeatedly failed to detect the breaches.
notes: Conclusion PDF parsed (SCANS.md demand-scan item 1); this is the 25/14 conclusion the 2026-09-03 pass named as approved-but-unpublished (k25014.pdf was 404 then, 200 now). Responsible bodies: IKEM, and the Health Ministry as its founder, which NKU tells to ensure effective control of IKEM's management. Approved by the NKU Kolegium at its XII. session on 17 August 2026, resolution 9/XII/2026; NKU press release of 14 September 2026 (the record date), not yet fetched by the scripted nku feed. Scale 0 because the finding is about one institute; the 345-order splitting of IT services under procurement thresholds is the transferable pattern, recorded here as the finding and not generalised. Kept by money 3.
quote: Kontrola prověřila 30 veřejných zakázek v celkové hodnotě 578,7 mil. Kč. U poloviny z nich, v celkové hodnotě 380,1 mil. Kč, IKEM porušil právní předpisy.

title: Small-municipality state administration — 69% call misdemeanour agenda the heaviest burden, 90% of larger towns underfunded
money_note: The report measures perceived burden and funding sufficiency, not amounts; no figure is published
summary: An ombudsman survey of 2,191 type-I and 140 type-II municipalities found that about two thirds rate misdemeanour proceedings (69 percent) and public guardianship (61 percent) as the most burdensome delegated state agendas, and roughly two fifths also see those same agendas as of little benefit to citizens. The state's contribution for delegated administration is judged insufficient or only partly sufficient by 61 percent of municipalities above 3,000 inhabitants and 90 percent above 10,000, and no municipality above 10,000 called the ministries' methodological support sufficient for all agendas.
notes: Ombudsman ESO checklist source (SCANS.md demand-scan item 4), research report Vykon statni spravy na malych obcich, sp. zn. 3626/2024/VOP, c. j. KVOP-12306/2026, issued 10 March 2026. Survey April-May 2025: all 183 type-II municipalities (140 answered, 77 percent) and all 6,075 type-I municipalities (2,191 answered, 36 percent). Found via the ESO search now that the method works (see manifest: session cookie + POST /Nalezene/GetTableContent). Pairs with reg-verejne-opatrovnictvi-prenos-2027 (the guardianship agenda transfer), which is the regulatory answer to one of the two agendas this report names; the misdemeanour agenda has no such record. Delegated powers are mandated by law, so recurrence 3.
quote: Za nejvíce zatěžující považují přibližně dvě třetiny obcí agendy projednávání přestupků (69 %) a veřejného opatrovnictví (61 %).

title: Patient complaints to regional authorities — 7% upheld, and most authorities struggle to find independent experts
money_note: No amount at stake is published; the only money figure is expert pay of 250-800 CZK an hour (average 409 CZK), which is a cost rate, not a market value
summary: An ombudsman survey of the regional authorities and ministries that handle second-instance complaints about healthcare providers found that only 7 percent (147 of 2,115) of complaints filed in 2018-2022 were upheld, with rates per inhabitant varying almost ninefold between regions. 53 percent of the authorities report obstacles in securing independent medical experts in most specialties and 59 percent in convening independent expert commissions, citing experts' workload, fear of conflict with complainants and low pay averaging 409 CZK an hour.
notes: Ombudsman ESO checklist source (SCANS.md demand-scan item 4), research report Setreni stiznosti ve zdravotnictvi spravnimi organy, sp. zn. 12344/2022/VOP, c. j. KVOP-1559/2025, issued 13 January 2025. Older than the last broad pass but never harvested: the ESO search could not be read until this pass (the 2026-09-03 control failed). Also from the summary: in 52 percent of authorities one or two staff handle the complaint agenda and only about a quarter have a dedicated specialist; fewer than half (47 percent) can get an in-house legal opinion without difficulty. The complaint mechanism is set by zakon o zdravotnich sluzbach (2012), so recurrence 3.
quote: Více než polovina správních orgánů (53 %) uvedla, že vnímá překážky při zajišťování nezávislých odborníků ve většině oborů.

title: Foreign-language e-submissions to Czech authorities — half of municipal offices lack the language staff
money_note: No amount published; about a fifth of respondents name missing money for external translation as a barrier, without a figure
summary: An ombudsman survey of 336 respondents across ministries, supervisory bodies, regional offices and 159 municipal offices with extended powers (90 percent return) found that 54 to 71 percent of offices received foreign-language electronic submissions in 2019-2023, yet 59 percent of the municipal offices answer only in Czech and 38 percent demand a translation. Insufficient language skills are the top barrier, named by 49 percent of municipal-office respondents and 41 to 43 percent at ministries and regional offices, with about a fifth also citing no budget for external translation.
notes: Ombudsman ESO checklist source (SCANS.md demand-scan item 4), research report Cizojazycna elektronicka podani, sp. zn. 3572/2023/VOP, c. j. KVOP-31121/2025, Brno 14 July 2025. Never harvested before: the ESO search could not be read until this pass. The ombudsman's own standard is that an office may not ignore a submission for not being in Czech and should at minimum respond in English; the survey shows the municipal tier furthest from it (47 percent have no foreign-language website). Also: 9 to 19 percent of respondents already use machine translation.
quote: Téměř polovina respondentů (49 %) uvedla, že považuje za problém nedostatečně jazykově vybavený personál úřadu.
